sourceScope: James Clear, Atomic Habits: An Easy & Proven Way to Build Good Habits & Break Bad Ones, Avery, 2018, ISBN 9780735211292. The title/creator fields of scoped local EPUB metadata were checked: no matching Clear/Atomic Habits edition was found; no unrelated library titles were used. No complete English volume or authorized RU translation was read. Evidence is the official author summary plus fifteen author pages carrying actual book-excerpt text, and two checked publisher excerpts (PRH Education on small changes; PRH on tracking/identity). Retained passages were read for systems, identity, the four-stage loop, all four laws and inversions, scorecard, specific time/place, habit stacking, visible environment, temptation bundling, action versus preparation, Two-Minute Rule, automation, tracking/recovery, manageable difficulty and boredom. Concrete retained cases are British cycling (as Clear’s attributed account), his wife’s classroom names, Thorndike’s cafeteria, Ronan Byrne’s bike/Netflix, Clear’s password restriction, a short-gym-visit reader and Steve Martin. The evidence map names the direct URL and passage for each retained link. This supports a concise central-method arc, not a full-edition or line-by-line translation certificate. No subscriber/customer-only resources were used; incomplete/unverified PDF search results were not relied upon.

unresolvedIssues: This deliberately concise account omits secondary cases and topics not fully checked here, including the detailed habit contract, genetic differences, the full social-norms treatment and the complete reflection/review chapter. It does not claim to replace every chapter or certify complete-book/authorized-translation fidelity.

The public author pages are excerpts selected and sometimes adapted by Clear, not a complete 2018 edition. Modern scientific efficacy of every underlying study was not separately established; examples are attributed to Clear. No numerical guarantee or new health procedure is made.
